I added the `originVerify` option to the existing `apps/api/src/routes.ts`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes (124 tests, 0 failures).

- **`AppOptions`** now has `originVerify?: string | undefined`, placed between `profiles` and `buildInfo` as in the spec. Its doc comment says what it is: the shared secret CloudFront sends as `X-Origin-Verify`. It also covers the 403 `{ "error": "Forbidden." }` rejection, the `/health` exemption, the check running before CORS, auth and every route, and that `undefined` means no check.
- **`createApp`** now also takes `originVerify` as a parameter, matching the spec's signature. A new doc comment says it throws an Error whose message contains "originVerify" when the value is empty or has leading or trailing whitespace. The function body is exactly as it was, so the check itself is still unimplemented: whoever builds it has to add the middleware there.
- **Nothing else changed.** `AuthVariables` and `AppEnv` are untouched, and `AppEnv` is still not exported, as before. The spec adds no new constants or functions, so there are none. The header name, 403 status and body text are literal values the tests check.

Exported names added: none (the only addition is the `originVerify` field on the existing `AppOptions`, plus the matching `createApp` parameter).

I wrote the suite in `apps/api/test/aws-deploy.test.ts`. It compiles cleanly with `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and running it gives **23 passing and 35 failing**.

One thing differs from what you described: the seam's `createApp` doesn't throw `not implemented`. It accepts `originVerify` and ignores it. So every test where the app should behave as it does today already passes. That covers the "no check installed" cases, requests carrying the matching header, the `/health` exemption, header-name casing and whitespace stripping. Every test that expects a 403 or a construction-time throw fails, which is exactly the work left to implement.

**Coverage:** each of the 29 scenarios (7 `@happy`, 11 `@unhappy`, 9 `@boundary`, 2 `@concurrency`) gets two tests. One is its main path, running every row of its examples table where it has one. The other is one boundary case that follows directly from the spec, such as:
- a tab-padded header value
- a value whose only difference is the case of one letter
- `DELETE /health`
- `/Health`
- a secret with a doubled interior space
- the reverse order for the statelessness checks

Tests are flat, named `[kind-n] …`, and reuse the fake `Auth` from `routes.test.ts`, extended to count its calls. They use fixed fixtures throughout: no clock, network or filesystem.

**Spec conflict:** the spec gives the `/api/v1/todos` body as including `"userId":"user_1"`. It also says that response is unchanged from today, and today the in-memory store strips `userId` from what it returns. So the tests check the todo's `id`, `title`, `done` and `createdAt` and say nothing about `userId`. You may want to fix the spec's example body.

58 tests, in 1 file.

I wrote 33 hidden tests in `apps/api/test/hidden-aws-deploy/origin-verify.test.ts`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors, and all 33 tests fail against the seam as it stands.

**Checks I ran:**
- **Reference implementation:** I patched a copy of the compiled `routes.js` in the scratchpad (nothing in the repo changed). The hidden suite, the public suite and `routes.test.ts` all pass against it: 144 of 144.
- **Shortcuts:** I tried three shortcuts that pass the public suite. The hidden suite catches each one:
  - hard-coding the secrets the public suite uses: 5 hidden tests fail;
  - checking only space and trailing tab when refusing a padded secret: 1 hidden test fails;
  - accepting a value when any comma-separated part matches: the public suite already catches this (1 failure), and the hidden suite adds 4 more.

**What the hidden suite adds:**
- **Other secrets:** a one-character secret, a 362-character one, one containing `", "`, and interior tabs and punctuation. Each app must also refuse the Background's secret, which defeats hard-coding.
- **Near misses:** same-length values, extra prefixes and suffixes, and repeated headers in any order or count. A single literal `"wrong, s3cret-Value"` is also rejected.
- **Same answers as no check:** with the matching header, 17 routes (including the email and username routes) must return the same status and body as an app built without `originVerify`. CORS headers must match too.
- **Nothing runs before the check:** after a rejected request, `getSession`, `auth.handler` and the email/profile stores must all have been called zero times. Rejected responses and preflights must carry no `Access-Control-*` header at all.
- **No-auth app:** the check runs there too, for unknown routes, `/health`, other methods and lookalike paths.
- **Construction:** `createApp` must refuse secrets padded with `\t`, `\n` or `\r\n`, or made only of whitespace, with and without auth.
- **Load:** 30 overlapping requests to one app, and 4 apps (including an unguarded and a no-auth one) asked at once with every secret.
- **Sequences:** a run of 25 rejections, then alternating accepted and rejected requests.

**Something to check:** the current seam doesn't throw `not implemented`. It accepts `originVerify` and ignores it, which already gives the right result for an app with no secret (the happy-1 and happy-2 scenarios). To make every test fail against it, each "served" test first checks that a guarded app refuses `/version` with no header, so a 200 means the check passed rather than being absent. For happy-1 and happy-2, the check is that a guarded app refuses the same request the unguarded app serves.

33 tests, in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
